You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A held person's claims, and held claims, now count in every total again: claimed, due-totals,
overdue, the period figures, backing, the rollup lines. The only thing a hold still does is in the
pools: a held person gets no cut and their share is spread over the others, as before.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored

agent.result_text:
Holds no longer take anything out of the totals: held people's claims and held claims count again in claimed, due-totals, overdue, the period figures, backing and the rollup lines. The only thing a hold still does is in the pools: a held person gets no cut and their share is spread over the others. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests, and I ran it a second time after the last edits.

What changed:

- **Server:**
  - `Claim.counts` and `countsAsOf` no longer drop a claim because it is held.
  - `Person.heldOn(date, today)` now only checks retirement, so totals ignore a person's holds. That one change covers the rollup, statements and closing a period.
- **Front end:**
  - In `claims.ts`, `counts` and `countedOn` no longer check whether a claim is held.
  - In `people.ts`, `liveHolds` now gives back only the "retired" marker, not the person's own holds, so every total built on it counts held people's claims again.
- **Unchanged:**
  - Retirement works as before: once the retirement date is reached, an open claim not bound by a statement still drops out of the totals.
  - The pool-cut logic (`PoolResponse`, `PoolRepository`), the hold buttons, the "held"/"on hold" displays and the audit lines are untouched. The stored data needed no change.

I also updated the code comments that said a hold takes claims out of the totals.

probe.probe_text:
I read the code and changed nothing. I read the core myself (`Claim`, `ClaimFigure`, `ClaimStatus`, `ClaimNumbers`, `Settings`, `Person`, `Rollup`, and the front-end `claims.ts`, `rates.ts`, `people.ts`, `periods.ts`, `overdue.ts`). Two read-only searches covered the action, period, statement, rate, person, pool and sheet classes. I spot-checked a few of their findings (`SETTLED_DAYS = 7`, the reject/approve difference, the copy in `TakeStatement`), not all of them.

## 1. Figures and the rules behind them

### Per-claim figures (row `claim-row-<id>`)
| Shown (`data-testid`) | Rule, named as the code names it |
|---|---|
| `claim-number` | `ClaimNumbers.next`, given when the claim is opened (`NumberClaim`). The format is `FY<yyyy>-n`, using the fiscal year of the claim's **due-by** (`Settings.fiscalYearOf`, `fiscalStartMonth`). If `numbersByPeriod(today)` is on (today on or after `periodNumberingFrom`), the format is `<period>-n` instead, or `X-n` when no period contains the due-by. A claim in REVIEW gets no number until `ReviewClaim`. A number is never reused. Reassign and transfer renumber (`RenumberClaim`). |
| `claim-amount` | When the claim has lines, the amount must equal their total (`ApplyClaim`, `AddClaimLine`). A negative amount is a correction. |
| `claim-due` | Front end: `claimDue` in `rates.ts`. Back end: `ClaimFigure.withLate`. The steps: **(1)** if `settledDue` is set, show it (frozen). **(2)** Otherwise take the rate figure: `statedDue` if a statement bound it (`isBound`), else `amount × rate ÷ 100` rounded to 2 dp. The rate is `Rate.inForce` / `rateOn` for the person's grade on the claim's date (`gradeOn`), sheet level first, then parents (`MAX_LEVEL=3`), then the clone source. A forward-only rate applies only to claims whose id is above `addedAfter`; older claims use the version it `replaced`. **(3)** That figure is raised to `floorOn(date)` (default 1.00). A correction has no floor. **(4)** Add `late`. **(5)** With no rate the due is `n/a`, and n/a gets no floor. |
| Rounding | `Settings.rounding` / `roundsHalfUp`: the dated `rounding` setting in force on the claim's `roundDate`. If none is set, round half-up before `policyDate` (default: today) and half-even on or after it. A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects (`getRoundDate`, `correctedDate`). |
| Late charge | `ClaimFigure.late` / `lateAsOpen`; front end `lateCharge`. Only OPEN or PENDING claims that are not deferred, not a correction and not `waived` get one. Count from `overdueFrom(dueBy, grade, date)`, which is due-by plus the grade's `grace-<G>` days. For each full 30 days, add the `latePctOn` that boundary date (default 0.00) of the figure plus the charges so far (it compounds). Each step is rounded the way the claim rounds. A statement-bound `statedLate` overrides all of this. |
| `claim-due-by` | `fixDueBy`: the terms-th business day after the claim's date, skipping weekends and holidays. The terms are fixed when the claim is made (`Settings.termsFor`): the person's own dated terms, else the grade's `terms-<G>`, else the sheet's `terms` (default 14). Redating does **not** change it. `RefixDueBys` recomputes it when a holiday is added on or before the due-by, unless the claim is SETTLED or VOID. |
| `claim-overdue` | `isOverdue` (front end) or `Rollup.overdue`: OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, and `overdueFrom` is before today. |
| `claim-period` | `periodOf(periods, dueBy)`: a claim belongs to the period that contains its **due-by**, not its date. |
| `claim-deferred` | `showsDeferred`: shown whatever the status. `isDeferred` / `isDeferredOn` (OPEN, and today < `deferredUntil`) is what actually removes it from every total. |
| `claim-stated`, `statedDue`, `statedLate` | Set by `TakeStatement`. They are cleared by `CancelStatement`, `reassign` and `split`, and kept by `mergeTo`. |
| `claim-review-late` | `isReviewLate`: REVIEW, and `reviewOn + reviewSla` is before today. |
| `claim-late-entry` | Set when the claim was added while its period was soft-closed (`CheckClaimPeriod`). |
| Status | `ClaimStatus.canMoveTo`: DRAFT→REVIEW/OPEN/DELETED, REVIEW→OPEN, OPEN→PENDING/SETTLED, any non-final status→VOID, DELETED→DRAFT. |
| Other flags | `claim-held` is `toggleHold`; it changes no total and only matters to pool cuts. `claim-waived` is `waive`, once, steward only. `claim-reminded` is `remind`, once per sheet day; it escalates after `escalateAfter` days. `claim-batch` is `settleBatch`. `claim-proofs*` come from `addProof`. `claim-split-from` is set by `split`. `claim-opened-by` is set when the claim is opened. |

### Which claims count
- **`counts`** (due-total, overdue, period total): `Claim.counts` in the back end, `counts` in `claims.ts` in the front end.
  - SETTLED always counts.
  - OPEN and PENDING count, unless the person's retirement date has been reached (`retiredOn(today)`, built in the front end as `liveHolds`) and no statement binds the claim.
  - A claim deferred on today never counts.
  - DRAFT, REVIEW, VOID and DELETED never count.
  - **Person holds and claim holds do not exclude anything.** Several comments still say they do, for example the `Hold` type and `personOverdue` in the front end.
- **`countsClaimed`** (claimed figures): the same rule, and corrections are also left out.

### Per-person figures
- `person-claimed` (`sumAmounts`): the amounts of counting, non-correction claims, added in whole cents.
- `person-due-total` (`personDueTotal`; `Rollup.of` in the back end): `claimDue` for each counting claim, added up skipping n/a, then held to `capOn(today)` (`Settings.capped`).
  - It is `n/a` when the grade in force today has no rate today and no counting claim is "kept".
  - "Kept" means: it has `settledDue`, it has a bound non-n/a figure, it has a figure under a different grade, or it has a figure and is dated on or before today. The last condition is almost always true, so `n/a` is nearly unreachable.
- `person-excess` (`personExcess`): the uncapped total minus the cap, or 0.00.
- `person-settled-total` / `person-open-total` (`personSplitTotals`): the same figures split by status, before the cap.
- `person-overdue-count` / `person-overdue-total` (`personOverdue`).
- Ageing buckets (`personAged`): 0–30, 31–60 and 61+ days from the claim's date. Only open claims that count are included.
- `person-statement-count` / `person-stated-total`: `TakeStatement` binds every counting claim to its current figure and late charge, then sums `withLate` and caps it. `CancelStatement` (steward only) unbinds and restores the previous total.
- Period figures (`personPeriodDueTotal`, `personPeriodCarried`): claims whose due-by is in the period and that counted at `period.to`, using the status from the claim's log (`statusOn` / `countedOn`). The figure itself is the due as shown today. "Carried" adds OPEN or PENDING claims from earlier periods plus the imported opening balance.
- `person-cut-total`, pool cuts (`PoolResponse.cutsOf`):
  - Only paid when there is a pot and the active shares total exactly 100.00.
  - A retired or held member gets 0.00.
  - Cuts round half-even, and the remainder goes to the smallest cut.

### Sheet totals
- `rollup-claimed-total`: plain sum of the people's claimed figures.
- `rollup-due-total`, `rollup-overdue-total`, `header-due-total` and `consolidated-*` (`trimmedSumDue`): with 3 or more people, the single highest and single lowest are dropped.
- `classic-due-total`, `rollup-settled-total`, `rollup-open-total`, the summary per-grade totals and crew totals: plain sums, not trimmed.
- `classic-period-*`: counts each claim by its status now. A closed period shows its frozen figure.
- Audit (`Rollup.changesSince`): ROLLUP, TOTALS and ALERT lines, where ALERT fires when a person goes above `alertThreshold`.

### What is frozen, and when
- **Settle** (`SettleClaim`): `settledDue` is set to the floored figure plus the late charge at that moment. A settle as of a date (`on` ≤ today) recomputes everything as of that date (`dueAsOf`).
- **Approve**: freezes the figure as it is at approval.
- **Re-settle** (steward): overwrites `settledDue` with the figure as of today.
- **Statement**: freezes `statedDue` and `statedLate` while the claim stays open.
- **Close period** (`ClosePeriod.fix`): stores each person's totals, the period total and the carried figure. A soft close freezes the figures but still allows changes, which are marked `lateEntry`. A hard close makes `CheckClaimPeriod` refuse claims whose due-by is in the period.
  - `AutoClosePeriods` closes a period once `to + graceDays` is before a new today.
  - `ReopenPeriod` clears the frozen figures. A locked period cannot be reopened.

### Who may do what
- `Settings.allows(action, role)` uses the `perms` matrix, falling back to `standingRoles`: reassign, reopen and lock are steward only; everything else is clerk or steward. A viewer may never change anything (`CheckCanChange`).
- An active delegation makes the user a steward.
- **Settle:** a clerk settling above `clerkLimitFor(grade, today)` makes the claim PENDING instead. Whoever opened or last edited the claim may not settle it (`isOwnedBy`, `SelfSettleException`). If `needsProof` (due above the proof threshold, by grade, on the claim's date; `proofKinds` lists the kinds required), settling is refused.
- **Approve and reject:** a steward or the person's `approver` may do these. Approve has the self ban; reject does not.
- **Void:** a SETTLED claim may be voided only by a steward, and only within `SETTLED_DAYS = 7` (hardcoded). A void reason is required while the sheet has a list of reasons.
- **Steward only, hardcoded rather than in the matrix:** review, re-settle, redate, waive, flag, merge, transfer, clone, archive, cancel statement.
- **Opening a claim:** refused for a flagged person unless the user is a steward (`flagRefuses`). Refused without a note when the due is above the note threshold (`needsNote`). It goes to REVIEW when the due is above the review threshold (`needsReview`). It is refused when the person already has `cap` open claims in that period (`PeriodCaps.full`).

### What a date decides
- **Claim date:** the rate and grade, floor, late %, grace days, rounding mode, proof, note and review thresholds, and the retirement refusal (`retiredBefore`).
- **Day the claim is made:** the terms.
- **Sheet's today:** the clerk limit, the cap, deferral, the late-charge count, and the displayed grade.
- **Due-by:** the period and the number.
- **New claim with no date:** `entryDay` (the entry date setting, else today). `ApplyClaim` defaults to today instead.

### Imports and bulk actions
- **Import people:** updates existing people's grade (from today), terms (undated) and contact.
- **Import rates:** one rate save per line. A rate saved with a from-date on or after today is forward-only.
- **Import openings:** adds to the person's carried opening balance; it does not replace it.
- **Paste:** opens each claim as the Open button would. It is not truly all-or-nothing: earlier lines are already saved when a later line fails. Paste and quick-add skip `CheckCorrection`.
- **Bulk settle:** all or nothing.
- **Bulk void, redate, open and reassign:** skip claims that fail individually. Bulk reassign allows the same person, which the single reassign refuses.
- **Holds** affect only pool cuts. **Retirement** removes unbound open claims from totals from the retirement date on.

## 2. How hard it was to follow

It is scattered and tangled, not in one clear place. The figure rules are written twice, in Java (`ClaimFigure`, `Rollup`, and a third copy in `TakeStatement`) and in TypeScript (`rates.ts`, `claims.ts`, `overdue.ts`, `periods.ts`), and that TypeScript is used again across about ten screen components. The permission and freeze rules are spread over about 150 one-method step classes and their YAML wiring, with stale comments (holds "count in no total") and small inconsistencies, so a new developer would have to read both stacks side by side to be sure what a figure is.
